chunks.text: So suppose we have a point mass particle of mass m moving

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: with velocity vector v.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: We can introduce a quantity we call the momentum of that

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: particle.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: I'll label it with the symbol p.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And it's equal to the product of the mass times of velocity.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: This is something you've undoubtedly seen before.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Now let's think about the dimensions of a momentum

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: for a moment.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So dimensionally, momentum has units of mass times of velocity.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And so that's in SI units, the units of mass are kilograms.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And then the units of velocity are meters per second.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: You can also express momentum dimensionally

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: as the product of a force times time.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And so again, in SI units, the force

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: or the Newton and the units of time is the second.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So these are the SI units from a momentum,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: two different ways of writing the same dimensions.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Now we've seen that for a single particle,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: we can write Newton's second law as the force

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: is equal to the mass times the acceleration.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Or equivalently, we can write that as the mass times

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: the time derivative of the acceleration dv dt.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Now if m is a constant, then I can rewrite this as f

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: is equal to the time derivative of mass times velocity

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: or equivalently as the time derivative of momentum,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: since mv is just equal to p.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So I actually want to express this,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: I'm actually going to put it in a box,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: because it's very important that I can write Newton's second

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: law instead of f equals mA as f equals the time derivative

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: of the momentum.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And this is actually where we'll see the momentum becomes

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: very useful, because it turns out that this form of Newton's

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: because it's applicable not just to a single point mass,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: but also to a more complicated system,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: a system consisting of many masses,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: or a system where the mass is changing,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: where the mass is flowing as in a fluid,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: and all of those cases, this form of Newton's second law

chunks.text: Whenever we have a relation involving a derivative like this,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: which can be very useful, and give us

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: a different way of looking at the same information.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So let's take a look at that.

chunks.text: So if I take this equation and integrate both sides

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: as the integral of f with respect to time

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: with respect to time.

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: I'll go from time t1 to time t2 on both sides here.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Now, this right-hand side is just, so the integral of dp dt

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And that is just the change in the momentum vector going

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: Now, this integral on the left-hand side, we give a special name.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: We call this the impulse.

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: but rather just on the integral of f.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And suppose I had some complicated function that looked

chunks.title: motion

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: The impulse is just the area under this curve.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: It's the integral of this function.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: That's the impulse.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And the change in the momentum depends only on the area

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: under this curve and not on the detailed shape of the curve.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So what that means is that I can define an average force

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: by choosing a constant force that has the same area,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: as this example on the left.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So suppose I calculated that.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And there's some constant force here.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: I'll call this f average going over the same time interval.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: The average force is that constant force,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: which has the same area as the area under my f of t.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So in other words, f average times delta t, which

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: is the area on the right-hand side here,

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: is equal to the integral of f of t dt

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: integrated from 0 to delta t, which is the area under this right hand

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: curve.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And so my average force is just that integral f of t dt divided by delta t.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: And this is integrated from 0 to delta t.

chunks.title: motion
chunks.text: So that's my average force.
